CAFETERIA LESSON · CAFETERIA · AGES 2–5 YEARS

Pudding — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches pudding as dessert physics — it wobbles, it holds a line, it wiggles when tapped — with a finger-drawing finale.

What is this?

Pudding is milk thickened with starch into a soft, spoonable cream, chilled in a cup until it sets. Chocolate is the tray’s classic, with a gentle peak on top.

What does it mean?

Find the pudding is a search among the shelf’s cups — applesauce is gold, yogurt has a label, and pudding is the brown one with the peak. Three cups, three tells.

What does the child need to know?

The wobble is the experiment: tap the table and watch the surface ripple. Dessert that responds to percussion is the happiest science demonstration in the building.

Why this matters

Pudding is the soft-food finisher — the last course for brand-new eaters and the comfort cup for everyone after — and it teaches solid-versus-liquid without saying so.

What it teaches

Solid-liquid curiosity, finger-drawing control, and three-cup visual sorting.

Words to learn

puddingwobblesetthickcupchocolate

Say this to your child

“Brown and soft, with a little mountain on top — pudding! Tap the table... look, it wobbles! Pudding is milk that learned to hold still, but only mostly. Draw a line with your finger... lick it... draw again. Dessert physics!”

Step by step

  1. Show the card and find the peak — the soft mountain on top. Sort the three cups by color: gold applesauce, brown pudding, labeled yogurt. Then tap the table beside a real pudding and watch it wobble — name the wobble! Draw a finger line across the top, lick the line, and draw again. End by asking what would happen with no spoon.

Look closer at the picture

Watch the finger line: it holds for a second, then slowly heals. The healing is the lesson — pudding is between solid and liquid, and children test it repeatedly.

Ask your child

Which cup is the pudding? What happened when we tapped? What did you draw? Is pudding hard or soft?

What your child can say or do

Wobble! / The brown one. / I drew a road. / It fixed itself!

Out in the real world

Pudding cups ride every lunchbox and hospital tray — the wobble test works anywhere a cup and a table meet, which is every dessert from here on.

Try it together

Cup lineup: three real cups — applesauce, yogurt, pudding — tap each one and rate the wobble from still to jiggly. Rank them, then eat the experiment in order.

Understanding check

Ask what pudding does when the table taps. Wobbles, wiggles, shakes — any motion word passes.

This lesson pairs with the Pudding flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Cafeteria.
